It begins with the LLO family of recalibration functions, defined by parameters δ and γ, which map input probabilities to recalibrated ones. These functions are evaluated using a Bayesian calibration check based on Bernoulli likelihood and BIC approximations to compute the posterior probability of calibration. The boldness-recalibration process then selects the optimal LLO parameters that maximize the standard deviation of the recalibrated probabilities, subject to a minimum calibration threshold. This ensures forecasts are both informative (sharp) and reliable (calibrated). Optimization failures occur when likelihood becomes degenerate, and extremization risks overconfidence unless bounded by log-loss or CLV metrics. The method is sensitive to model priors and assumes independence of Bernoulli trials.
